bull.argument: The filing shows a company compounding its core business while funding its future. Consolidated net sales rose 4.7% to $706.4 billion in fiscal 2026, and Walmart U.S. comparable sales grew 4.3% with eCommerce contributing about 4.3 points. Operating income reached $29.8 billion and consolidated net income rose to $22.3 billion, with EPS of $2.73 versus $2.41. Free cash flow increased to $14.9 billion from $12.7 billion even as capital expenditures rose $2.9 billion to support omnichannel growth, and management approved a new $30.0 billion repurchase authorization and a 5% dividend increase. The risk factors are extensive, but many describe generic exposures (tariffs, cyber threats, litigation) that the company has so far absorbed without a material adverse effect on operating results. Management's stated priority of returning capital while investing heavily in automation is a credible case that the spending is earning returns. Return on investment remained high at 15.1%.

claims.claim: Walmart U.S. comparable sales growth was driven by eCommerce contribution.
claims.quote: Walmart U.S. eCommerce sales positively contributed approximately 4.3% and 2.9% to comparable sales for fiscal 2026 and 2025, respectively.

claims.claim: Free cash flow rose despite higher capital spending.
claims.quote: Free cash flow for fiscal 2026 increased when compared to fiscal 2025 due to an increase in cash provided by operating income, lower cash tax payments and timing of certain payments, partially offset by an increase of $2.9 billion in capital expenditures

claims.claim: Management approved a larger buyback authorization after the fiscal year.
claims.quote: In February 2026, the Board of Directors approved a new $30.0 billion share repurchase authorization

bear.argument: The filing shows margin and return pressure beneath the headline growth. Operating income as a percentage of net sales fell to 4.2% from 4.4%, and operating income rose only about 1.6% ($29.8B vs $29.3B) on 4.7% net sales growth. Operating expenses rose to 20.9% of net sales from 20.7%, driven by a $0.9 billion self-insured liability charge and a $0.7 billion PhonePe share-based charge. ROI fell to 15.1% from 15.5%, and management says the rise in invested capital comes from higher capital spending. Free cash flow of $14.9 billion is also flattered by lower cash taxes and payment timing, and capital expenditures are guided up again to $25-27 billion for fiscal 2027. Meanwhile, the risk factors warn that investments in eCommerce and AI may hurt results in the short term and may not deliver the anticipated benefits, and that tariffs and litigation could be material. Buybacks of $8.1 billion and a $30.0 billion authorization are being funded while short-term borrowings rose to $6.6 billion and the working capital deficit widened to $22.6 billion.

claims.claim: Operating margin declined, and operating expenses rose as a share of sales.
claims.quote: Operating income as a percentage of net sales 4.2 % 4.4 %

claims.claim: Management expects capital spending to rise again, increasing reinvestment needs.
claims.quote: For the fiscal year ending January 31, 2027 ("fiscal 2027"), we project capital expenditures will be approximately $25 billion to $27 billion

claims.claim: The company warns that its large technology and eCommerce investments may not deliver expected benefits.
claims.quote: there can be no assurance that these investments will deliver the anticipated benefits

bull.argument: The bear's margin points are real, but they describe a company spending through a transition rather than a deteriorating one. Operating income did rise $0.5 billion to $29.8 billion, and the 13 basis point margin dip is explicitly attributed to identifiable items: a $0.9 billion self-insured liability charge and a $0.7 billion non-cash PhonePe share-based charge that the filing says provided no tax benefit. Strip out those one-time-style items and the underlying business is expanding, with Walmart U.S. operating income up $1.3 billion and gross profit rate up 22 basis points. Free cash flow rose to $14.9 billion even after $2.9 billion more capex, so the spending is being funded internally. The ROI decline to 15.1% reflects a higher capital base for omnichannel build-out, and the filing reports ROI still near 15%. Short-term borrowings of $6.6 billion are modest against $15.0 billion of undrawn U.S. credit lines and AA-rated long-term debt. The buyback and dividend increase reflect confidence in cash generation.

claims.claim: Walmart U.S. operating income grew, offsetting the consolidated margin pressure.
claims.quote: segment operating income increased $1.3 billion and $1.7 billion for fiscal 2026 and 2025

claims.claim: Liquidity remains supported by undrawn credit and strong ratings.
claims.quote: We also have $15.0 billion of various undrawn committed lines of credit in the U.S. as of January 31, 2026

claims.claim: The PhonePe charge was non-cash and gave no tax benefit, distorting the effective tax rate rather than core operations.

bear.argument: The bull's adjusted view depends on treating the $0.9 billion self-insured liability charge as one-time, but the filing describes it as a trend: "rising costs to resolve claims across retail and related industries." Operating income grew only about 1.7% on 4.7% sales growth, and the margin fell from 4.4% to 4.2%. Walmart International operating income fell $0.4 billion, and Sam's Club was roughly flat, so the gain rests on one segment. Free cash flow improved mainly because of lower cash taxes and payment timing, which the filing does not describe as recurring. Capital expenditures are guided up again to $25-27 billion for fiscal 2027, and ROI fell to 15.1% as invested capital grew faster than returns. Working capital deficit widened to $22.6 billion, and buybacks of $8.1 billion exceeded the $7.5 billion of dividends paid. Management also concedes these AI and eCommerce investments may not deliver their anticipated benefits.

claims.claim: The liability charge is described as a rising, industry-wide cost trend, not a one-time item.
claims.quote: higher self-insured general liability claims expense in the U.S. of approximately $0.9 billion, influenced by rising costs to resolve claims across retail and related industries

claims.claim: Free cash flow improvement was driven partly by lower cash taxes and timing, not operating gains alone.
claims.quote: Free cash flow for fiscal 2026 increased when compared to fiscal 2025 due to an increase in cash provided by operating income, lower cash tax payments and timing of certain payments

claims.claim: Management warns that technology and eCommerce investments may hurt near-term results and may not deliver expected benefits.
claims.quote: the cost of certain investments in eCommerce, technology, talent and automation, including any operating losses incurred for those initiatives, will adversely impact our financial performance in the short-term

judge.reasoning: Both sides cite verified quotes accurately, so evidence is roughly even. The bear better answers the bull's rebuttal by showing the $0.9B self-insured charge is described as an industry-wide rising trend rather than a one-time item, which undercuts the bull's 'strip out one-time items' framing. The bull's defense of the margin and FCF is reasonable but leans on segment gains and a 'one-time-style' characterization the filing does not support, so the bear edges the debate.
